title: 深谈中国的机器人革命内情(8)
desc: 深谈中国的机器人革命内情(8)

paragraphs.en: Chen combines the cautious pragmatism of an engineer with the techno-optimism of a founder.
paragraphs.zh: 陈亮兼具工程师审慎务实的思维，同时又怀揣创业者对科技发展的乐观期待。

paragraphs.en: Though he is clear-eyed about deep learning's limitations, he believes much of the assembly work in the factory will be close to fully automated by the mid-2030s.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他十分清楚深度学习技术存在诸多局限，但他认为到2030年代中期，工厂绝大多数装配工序都将基本实现全自动化。

paragraphs.en: Like many of his peers in the Chinese robotics industry, Chen views the displacement of human labour with detachment.
paragraphs.zh: 和国内机器人行业许多同行一样，陈亮对于人工被机器替代这件事看得十分淡然。

paragraphs.en: To him, the onrush of technology is no more contestable than the passage of time.
paragraphs.zh: 在他眼中，科技飞速发展就像时光流逝，是无法阻挡的大势。

paragraphs.en: When I pressed him to consider the social consequences of his work, he acknowledged that he and his business partners had discussed contingency plans for laid-off workers.
paragraphs.zh: 当我追问他这项技术带来的社会影响时，他坦言自己和合作伙伴讨论过被替代工人的安置预案。

paragraphs.en: Those who are higher-skilled could be used to train the next generation of robots, he said.
paragraphs.zh: 掌握较高技能的工人，可以转型去训练新一代机器人。

paragraphs.en: He did not say how he would deal with lower-skilled workers.
paragraphs.zh: 但他并未提及技能水平较低的工人该如何安置。

paragraphs.en: Back inside the Huawei factory, we reached a station where five to six workers huddled under the raised Huawei car, craning their necks to bolt screws and tightening connectors by hand.
paragraphs.zh: 回到华为生产车间，我们来到一处工位，五六名工人围在举升起来的汽车底盘下方，仰头手动拧紧螺丝、对接线路接头。

paragraphs.en: "Long-term, this causes spinal damage," Chen told me matter-of-factly.
paragraphs.zh: “长期做这种工作，很容易造成脊椎损伤。”陈亮语气平淡地说道。

paragraphs.en: It was better that they be replaced by humanoids.
paragraphs.zh: 用人形机器人替代这类岗位其实是更好的选择。

paragraphs.en: There are 120 million workers in Chinese factories today, several million of whom, like the workers in front of me, had undertaken three to five years of vocational training.
paragraphs.zh: 目前中国工厂共有1.2亿产业工人，其中数百万人，就像眼前这些工人一样，接受过三到五年职业技能培训。

paragraphs.en: I asked Chen what this meant for their successors, those in middle school hoping to undergo training in advanced manufacturing now.
paragraphs.zh: 我问陈亮，这对于如今正在读中学、打算未来学习先进制造专业的年轻人意味着什么。

paragraphs.en: "They definitely need to change careers," said Chen.
paragraphs.zh: “他们肯定要更换职业赛道。”陈亮答道。

paragraphs.en: Decades ago, China's infrastructure build-out of apartment towers, skyscrapers and high-speed rail dazzled the world, but it masked a story of expropriated land, corruption and waste.
paragraphs.zh: 数十年前，中国大规模修建居民楼、摩天大楼与高铁基础设施，令世界为之惊叹，但背后也伴随着土地征用、贪腐与资源浪费等问题。

paragraphs.en: Today, something similar is happening.
paragraphs.zh: 如今相似的局面正在上演。

paragraphs.en: The vast build-outs of industries such as semiconductors, solar panels and electric vehicles are impressive to behold, but much of China's population, which is facing diminishing economic prospects and alarming youth unemployment, are now wondering what all that effort was for.
paragraphs.zh: 半导体、光伏、电动汽车等产业大规模扩张，成果亮眼，但国内大量民众经济前景承压，青年失业率居高不下，人们不禁开始质疑，如此大规模投入究竟意义何在。

paragraphs.en: Even those driving China's flagship industries sometimes bemoan their situation.
paragraphs.zh: 即便是国内龙头产业的从业者，有时也会感慨行业生存不易。

paragraphs.en: At his last company, which built machines for EV batteries, Chen worked 16-hour days and clients, who often delayed payments, demanded the impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 陈亮上一家企业主营动力电池生产设备，那时他每天工作十六小时，客户不仅经常拖欠尾款，还会提出各种不切实际的要求。

paragraphs.en: "Something that should take a month, they make you finish in 10 days," he told me.
paragraphs.zh: “本该一个月完工的项目，他们要求十天交付。”他对我说。

paragraphs.en: As government subsidies flood the robotics sector, Chen and his peers are bracing for the usual pattern: price wars and cost cutting manoeuvres that leave companies barely able to turn a profit.
paragraphs.zh: 随着各地政府大量补贴涌入机器人赛道，陈亮和同行们都做好了应对行业常态竞争的准备：价格战、压缩成本，企业利润被压到微薄。

paragraphs.en: A couple of weeks earlier, back at the warehouse in Guchi's Shanghai headquarters, Chen and I had watched the General Motors employees prepare to ship Chen's machines to the west.
paragraphs.zh: 几周前，在固智上海总部的仓库里，我和陈亮看着通用汽车的工作人员调试设备，这批设备即将发往海外。

paragraphs.en: Chen would shortly be travelling to the US, where he was planning to visit Tesla and General Motors to seek new business opportunities.
paragraphs.zh: 不久后陈亮计划前往美国，拜访特斯拉与通用汽车，开拓新的合作订单。

paragraphs.en: Under successive administrations, we have heard that the US is committed to decoupling from China, but the reality is more complicated.
paragraphs.zh: 美国历届政府都宣称要与中国脱钩，但现实情况远比口号复杂。

paragraphs.en: It is not just American businesses that need China; the reverse is also true.
paragraphs.zh: 不只是美国企业离不开中国市场，中国企业同样需要美国市场。

paragraphs.en: Chen told me that he'd learned a lot from working with GM: how American manufacturers approach process management – the protocols, safety standards and quality controls that, when followed correctly, eliminate errors before they happen.
paragraphs.zh: 陈亮表示，和通用汽车合作的经历让他收获良多：学习美方企业的流程管理体系，包括标准化流程、安全规范与质量管控体系，这套机制能从源头规避生产失误。

paragraphs.en: It has made his team more disciplined.
paragraphs.zh: 这段合作经历也让他的团队管理更加规范。

paragraphs.en: Working with Americans is "no longer optional, it's inevitable," Chen told me.
paragraphs.zh: 陈亮说，和美国企业合作“早已不是可选项，而是必然趋势”。

paragraphs.en: And besides, he added, "Americans pay on time."
paragraphs.zh: 除此之外，他补充道：“美方客户付款十分准时。”
